indicator.name: 10-Year / 2-Year Treasury Yield Spread
indicator.description: The difference between the 10-year and 2-year U.S. Treasury yields, measured in percentage points. It represents the slope of an important segment of the Treasury yield curve.
indicator.use: Monitor the slope of the U.S. Treasury yield curve and identify changes in the relationship between longer-term and shorter-term interest rates.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized measure of the 10-year versus 2-year Treasury yield differential for analyzing monetary policy expectations, economic conditions, and changes in the shape of the yield curve.
indicator.significance: The 10-year/2-year yield spread provides information about changing expectations for interest rates and economic conditions. Changes in the spread can indicate shifts in the relative pricing of short- and longer-term Treasury securities and are useful for interpreting the broader yield curve.

indicator.name: 10-Year Breakeven Inflation Rate
indicator.description: A market-based measure of expected average inflation over the next ten years, derived from the difference between nominal 10-year Treasury yields and 10-year Treasury inflation-indexed securities.
indicator.use: Monitor market-based inflation expectations and changes in the outlook for long-term inflation.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-derived measure of expected average inflation over a ten-year horizon for analyzing inflation expectations, Treasury markets, monetary policy, and financial conditions.
indicator.significance: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate reflects the inflation compensation implied by the pricing difference between nominal and inflation-indexed Treasury securities. Changes in the measure can provide information about shifts in market-based inflation expectations.

indicator.name: 10-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on U.S. Treasury securities with a constant maturity of ten years, quoted on an investment basis. It reflects market pricing for longer-term U.S. government borrowing and expectations about future economic and financial conditions.
indicator.use: Monitor long-term U.S. interest rates, Treasury market conditions, financial conditions, inflation and growth expectations, and changes in the cost of government borrowing.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the ten-year point on the U.S. Treasury yield curve for analyzing long-term interest rates, economic expectations, monetary policy transmission, and financial market conditions.
indicator.significance: The 10-year Treasury yield is a major benchmark for U.S. long-term interest rates and influences pricing across financial markets. Changes in the yield can reflect shifts in expectations for inflation, economic growth, monetary policy, and demand for government securities.

indicator.name: 2-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on U.S. Treasury securities with a constant maturity of two years, quoted on an investment basis. It reflects market expectations and pricing for short-term U.S. government borrowing.
indicator.use: Monitor short-term U.S. interest rates, Treasury market conditions, monetary policy expectations, and changes in the cost of government borrowing.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the two-year point on the U.S. Treasury yield curve for analyzing interest-rate expectations, monetary policy, financial conditions, and relationships across the yield curve.
indicator.significance: The two-year Treasury yield is closely connected to expectations for future monetary policy and short-term interest rates. Changes in the yield can provide information about shifts in interest-rate expectations and broader financial conditions.

indicator.name: 3-Month Treasury Bill Rate
indicator.description: The secondary market interest rate for U.S. Treasury bills with a three-month maturity, quoted on a discount basis. The series is reported daily and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor short-term U.S. Treasury interest rates and assess changes in money-market conditions, monetary policy expectations, and short-term government borrowing costs.
indicator.purpose: Provide a high-frequency measure of the three-month Treasury bill rate for analyzing short-term interest rates, monetary policy transmission, liquidity conditions, and the front end of the U.S. yield curve.
indicator.significance: The three-month Treasury bill rate is a key short-term interest-rate benchmark and reflects market pricing for very short-term U.S. government debt. Changes in the rate can provide information about short-term monetary and financial conditions and expectations surrounding Federal Reserve policy.

indicator.name: 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate
indicator.description: The average interest rate for 30-year fixed-rate mortgages in the United States, based on Freddie Mac's weekly Primary Mortgage Market Survey. The rate is reported weekly for the period ending Thursday and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor mortgage financing costs and assess how changes in interest rates affect housing affordability, home-buying demand, refinancing activity, and residential construction.
indicator.purpose: Provide a high-frequency measure of U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rates for analyzing housing-market conditions, household financing costs, interest-rate transmission, and the relationship between monetary and financial conditions and residential activity.
indicator.significance: Mortgage rates directly affect the financing cost of home purchases and refinancing. Changes in 30-year fixed mortgage rates can influence housing affordability, buyer demand, transaction activity, construction incentives, and the broader transmission of interest-rate conditions into the housing market.

indicator.name: AAII Investor Sentiment Survey
indicator.description: A weekly survey of individual investors measuring the percentage who expect the U.S. stock market to rise, remain essentially unchanged, or fall over the next six months. The dataset includes bullish, neutral, bearish, and bull-bear spread readings.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in individual-investor expectations, optimism, pessimism, uncertainty, and overall sentiment toward the U.S. stock market, including changes in the bull-bear spread.
indicator.purpose: Provide a direct survey-based measure of individual-investor expectations that complements market-derived sentiment indicators by capturing what retail investors expect the stock market to do over the following six months.
indicator.significance: The AAII Sentiment Survey provides a direct measure of individual-investor expectations rather than inferring sentiment from market prices or positioning. Changes in bullish, neutral, and bearish responses reveal shifts in optimism, pessimism, and uncertainty, while the bull-bear spread summarizes the balance between optimistic and pessimistic views. Extreme sentiment readings can provide useful context for assessing investor psychology and potential sentiment reversals, but the survey does not establish the future direction of the market.

indicator.name: Average Hourly Earnings
indicator.description: The average gross hourly earnings of all private-sector employees in the United States, including premium pay for overtime and late-shift work. The series is seasonally adjusted and reported in dollars per hour.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in average hourly earnings and assess wage pressures, household income conditions, labor-market trends, and potential inflationary pressures.
indicator.purpose: Provide a broad measure of average hourly earnings in the private sector for analyzing labor-market conditions, wage growth, household income, inflation pressures, and economic activity.
indicator.significance: Average hourly earnings provide information about changes in the average hourly compensation received by private-sector workers. Changes can help identify wage pressures and their potential relationship with consumer spending and inflation, although movements can also reflect changes in the composition of workers rather than changes in individual workers' earnings.

indicator.name: Building Permits
indicator.description: The number of new privately owned housing units authorized by building permits in permit-issuing places across the United States. The series is reported monthly as a seasonally adjusted annual rate and expressed in thousands of units.
indicator.use: Monitor authorized residential construction activity and assess changes in housing demand, construction intentions, and conditions in the housing market.
indicator.purpose: Provide a timely measure of new residential building permits for analyzing prospective construction activity, housing-market conditions, construction investment, and the effects of interest rates and financial conditions on housing demand.
indicator.significance: Building permits provide information about residential construction that has been authorized but may not yet have begun. Changes in permits can provide insight into prospective construction activity, builder intentions, housing demand, and the broader economic cycle.

indicator.name: Real GDP Growth
indicator.description: The quarterly percentage change in inflation-adjusted U.S. gross domestic product from the preceding period, reported at an annual rate. The series is seasonally adjusted and measures changes in real economic output.
indicator.use: Monitor the pace of change in inflation-adjusted U.S. economic output and identify periods of economic expansion, slowing growth, or contraction.
indicator.purpose: Provide a published measure of quarterly real GDP growth for analyzing economic momentum, business-cycle conditions, and changes in aggregate economic activity.
indicator.significance: Real GDP growth measures changes in inflation-adjusted economic output and provides a broad indicator of economic momentum. Changes in the growth rate can help identify shifts between stronger and weaker periods of economic activity and changes in the business cycle.

indicator.name: CBOE Volatility Index
indicator.description: A market-based measure of expected near-term volatility in U.S. stock markets derived from stock index option prices. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in market-implied expectations for near-term equity-market volatility and identify shifts in financial-market uncertainty and risk conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of expected near-term stock-market volatility for analyzing investor risk expectations, market stress, financial conditions, and changes in market sentiment.
indicator.significance: The VIX reflects volatility expectations implied by stock index option prices. Changes in the index provide information about shifts in expected near-term equity-market volatility and can help contextualize changes in broader financial-market risk conditions.

indicator.name: CFTC Bitcoin Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of Bitcoin futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates Bitcoin futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Money, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable.
indicator.use: Track changes in Bitcoin futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including shifts in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Bitcoin futures and how their exposure changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC Bitcoin futures positioning provides a structured view of institutional, leveraged, dealer, and other trader exposure to Bitcoin through regulated futures markets. Changes in open interest reveal changes in futures-market participation, while changes in long and short positions show how each trader group is adjusting directional exposure. Separating trader classifications allows the intelligence system to distinguish institutional and leveraged positioning from dealer activity and aggregate nonreportable participation when analyzing Bitcoin market structure and sentiment.

indicator.name: Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index
indicator.description: A daily composite index from Alternative.me measuring crypto-market sentiment on a scale from 0 to 100, where lower values represent greater fear and higher values represent greater greed. Alternative.me derives the index from multiple sentiment-related inputs, including Bitcoin volatility, market momentum and volume, social media activity, surveys, Bitcoin dominance, and Google Trends. Alternative.me's published methodology currently identifies the index as Bitcoin-focused.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in aggregate crypto-market sentiment using Alternative.me's composite Fear & Greed Index and its fear-to-greed classification.
indicator.purpose: Provide a standardized daily measure of market sentiment that can be used to identify shifts between fear, neutrality, and greed in the crypto market.
indicator.significance: The Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index combines multiple market and sentiment signals into a single 0-to-100 measure. Alternative.me's published methodology assigns 25% weight to volatility, 25% to market momentum and volume, 15% to social media, 15% to surveys, 10% to Bitcoin dominance, and 10% to Google Trends, although Alternative.me currently states that its surveys are paused. The index therefore captures several dimensions of market behavior rather than directly measuring investor sentiment through a single survey. It can be analyzed alongside price trends, volatility, trading volume, derivatives positioning, funding rates, market breadth, Bitcoin dominance, and other sentiment indicators to provide broader context for changes in crypto-market conditions.
